title: 2017 AMC 10A Problem 24
statement: For certain real numbers \(a,\) \(b,\) and \(c,\) the polynomial \[g(x) = x^3 + ax^2 + x + 10\] has three distinct roots, and each root of \(g(x)\) is also a root of the polynomial \[ \begin{aligned} f(x) &= x^4 + x^3 \\ &\quad {}+ bx^2 + 100x + c. \end{aligned} \] What is \(f(1)?\)

solutions.text:
Because the three distinct roots of the cubic \(g\) are also roots of the monic quartic \(f,\) we can write \[f(x)=g(x)(x-r)\] for some real number \(r.\)

The coefficient of \(x\) in this product is \(10-r,\) so \(10-r=100\) and \(r=-90.\) The coefficient of \(x^3\) is \(a-r,\) so \(a-r=1\) and \(a=-89.\)

Therefore, \[\begin{aligned} f(1)&=g(1)(1-r)\\ &=(1-89+1+10)(91)\\ &=(-77)(91)\\ &=-7007. \end{aligned}\]

Thus, C is the correct answer.
hints: Because the roots of \(g\) are roots of \(f\), factor \(f\) by \(g\)
Compare the \(x^3\) and \(x\) coefficients to find the extra root and \(a\)
